source: D. R. Sarumi's Notes on Civil Litigation (draft by AI from the notes; legal reviewer to check); Q41–Q45 are problem questions built from the points of earlier cases (2026-10-24)

questions.question: Once I file a case at the FCT High Court, can the court push it to ADR even if I did not ask for it?
mustInclude: Originating processes are screened for ADR suitability upon acceptance for filing in Abuja
Where appropriate the chief judge may refer the case to the Abuja Multi-Door Court House or other ADR institutions
authorities: Order 2, Rule 7 of the High Court of Federal Capital Abuja (Civil Procedures) Rules 2018
questions.sourcePhrase: be screened for suitability for ADR, and where it is considered appropriate

questions.question: If I lose at arbitration, can the High Court just replace the award with its own decision?
mustInclude: An arbitral award can be set aside
The court cannot substitute the award with its own decision
questions.sourcePhrase: an award can be set aside, but the court cannot substitute

questions.question: The defendant raised an objection to jurisdiction halfway through trial. Can the judge leave it for final judgment, and what order is made if jurisdiction is lacking?
mustInclude: Jurisdiction can be raised at any stage by either party or by the court suo motu
An objection on jurisdiction must be heard first, otherwise the proceedings become a nullity
The proper order where a court lacks jurisdiction is to strike out
questions.sourcePhrase: objection on jurisdiction, it must be heard first

questions.question: How many justices can the Supreme Court have, and how long must someone have been at the bar to be appointed?
mustInclude: CJN and Justices not exceeding 21
Not less than 15 years at the bar
questions.sourcePhrase: Not less than 15 years at the bar

questions.topic: Transfer of wrongly filed cases: Abuja vs Lagos High Court
questions.question: The FCT High Court can transfer a case filed in the wrong court. Can the Lagos High Court do the same?
mustInclude: The Abuja Rules 2018 empower the FCT High Court to transfer cases wrongly commenced in it to the appropriate court
The Lagos High Court does not have an equivalent rule
questions.sourcePhrase: the Lagos High Court does not have an equivalent rule

questions.question: My client lost at the National Industrial Court. Can he appeal to the Court of Appeal as of right?
mustInclude: Appeal lies as of right from the NICN to the Court of Appeal in matters of enforcement of fundamental rights
In all other cases appeal is with leave of court
The Court of Appeal decision is final on civil matters arising from the NICN
questions.sourcePhrase: appeal lies as of right from the decisions of NICN

questions.question: Which rule on class actions is wider, the Abuja one or the Lagos one, and why?
mustInclude: Abuja is wider because it also includes tort
Order 13 Rule 15(3) Abuja has no equivalent in Order 15 Rule 13 Lagos
The class representative is appointed by the court
questions.sourcePhrase: Abuja is wider because it also includes tort

questions.question: I want to sue on behalf of my client's whole family over family land. Do I need leave of court first, and how do I apply?
mustInclude: Leave is not mandatory for claimants, but for defendants it appears required and desirable
Application is by motion ex parte with affidavit showing consent of the persons represented
The representative capacity must be pleaded
questions.sourcePhrase: Leave of court is not mandatory, for claimants

questions.question: How do I name a registered club (incorporated trustees) as claimant? Do I list each trustee?
mustInclude: Incorporated trustees sue or defend through their trustees
The names of the individual trustees are not mentioned
questions.sourcePhrase: the names of the individual trustees are not mentioned

questions.question: Who can bring third party proceedings, and what is the procedure?
mustInclude: Brought by a defendant only, or a claimant who is a defendant to a counterclaim
By motion ex parte with affidavit and written address
After leave, serve the order granting leave, the third party notice and copies of the processes
questions.sourcePhrase: Special proceedings brought by a defendant only

questions.question: The contract was to be performed in Ikeja but I filed in the Lagos judicial division. Is my suit fatally defective?
mustInclude: Judicial divisions are mainly for administrative convenience and non-compliance is non-fatal
Actions on contracts go to the division where the contract ought to have been performed or where the defendant resides or carries on business
questions.sourcePhrase: for administrative convenience and non-compliance is non-fatal

questions.question: My client sued without serving a pre-action notice the statute requires. Is the whole suit automatically void?
mustInclude: Pre-action notice is a condition precedent to be checked before suing
Non-service of pre-action notice is a procedural jurisdictional issue that can be waived
questions.sourcePhrase: Effect of non-service of pre-action notice

questions.topic: Pre-action counselling: Abuja vs Lagos sanctions
questions.question: What happens to counsel who files a false pre-action certificate in Abuja, compared with a false Form 01 in Lagos?
mustInclude: In Abuja the sanction for a false declaration or frivolous action is payment of costs of the action by counsel
In Lagos a false statement in Pre-Action Protocol Form 01 is perjury, a criminal offence
Lagos requires a prior attempt at settlement by written memorandum; the Abuja certificate does not specifically require one
questions.sourcePhrase: payment of costs of the action by counsel

questions.question: For a land dispute in Lagos, what must the letter of claim contain and how long does the defendant have to respond?
mustInclude: Letter of claim with supporting documents stating root of title and description of property
Defendant responds within 30 days
Claimant responds to any proposal within 7 days
questions.sourcePhrase: Letter of claim with supporting documents stating root of title

questions.question: The annual rent is N8 million but total arrears are N15 million. Can a Lagos Magistrate Court hear the recovery of premises and the arrears?
mustInclude: Jurisdiction covers premises whose annual rental value does not exceed N10,000,000 at filing
The claimant may also claim arrears of rent and mesne profits even if the total exceeds N10,000,000
It is the annual rent that is considered, not the total arrears
authorities: s. 28 of the Magistrate Court of Lagos State, 2009
questions.sourcePhrase: the annual rent that is considered and not the total

questions.question: My client was served an ordinary summons in a Lagos Magistrate Court. He wants to admit the debt and pay in instalments. What is the deadline?
mustInclude: Within 6 days of service he may notify the court (Form 4A) of admission and make a repayment proposal
The claimant may object within 3 days of receiving the proposal
If the claimant accepts, judgment is entered in the sum admitted
questions.sourcePhrase: within six (6) days of service of the summons on him notify

questions.question: In a Lagos Magistrate Court claim, how long does the claimant have to give further particulars once the defendant asks?
mustInclude: Defendant may demand further particulars within 6 days of service
Claimant must provide them within 2 days
If not provided, the court may order them, stay proceedings or strike out the suit
questions.sourcePhrase: provide the particulars within two (2) days

questions.question: Can I serve a Lagos Magistrate Court summons on a defendant who lives in Ogun State?
mustInclude: Summons cannot be served outside Lagos without the permission of the court
Application is ex parte supported by affidavit and written address
If granted, the defendant must be given at least 30 days to enter appearance
questions.sourcePhrase: the Defendant must be given at least 30 days to enter appearance

questions.question: Is the Small Claims limit in Abuja the same as in Lagos?
mustInclude: Lagos Small Claims limit is N5,000,000 excluding interest and cost
Abuja jurisdiction is 4 million
In Abuja the court is called the District Court and forms 3A, 3B and 5A are not in place
questions.sourcePhrase: The jurisdiction of the Court is 4 million

questions.question: How long do I have to appeal a Lagos Small Claims judgment?
mustInclude: Notice of appeal within 14 days of delivery of judgment (Form SCA 8B)
The whole appeal process shall not exceed 30 days
authorities: Article 15 of the Practice Direction on Small Claims 2023
questions.sourcePhrase: within 14 days of the delivery of the judgment

questions.question: What documents must I file with an originating summons in the Lagos High Court?
mustInclude: An affidavit setting out the facts relied on
All exhibits to be relied upon
A written address in support
Pre-action protocol Form 01
questions.sourcePhrase: A written address in support of the originating summons

questions.question: When do I start a case by petition instead of a writ?
mustInclude: Where prescribed by the applicable rules or legislation
Examples: election petitions, winding up of companies under CAMA 2020, matrimonial causes
The Lagos rules make no direct provision for petition
questions.sourcePhrase: Winding up of companies under CAMA 2020

questions.question: What happens in Abuja if I try to file a writ without the frontloaded documents, and how is that different from Lagos?
mustInclude: In Abuja the Registry shall not accept the originating process for filing if it is not frontloaded
In Lagos failure to frontload nullifies the action
In Abuja the claimant frontloads the certificate of pre-action counselling (Form 6) with the writ
questions.sourcePhrase: shall not accept originating process for filing if it is not frontloaded

questions.question: My Lagos writ was issued on 1 February and still has not been served by mid-August. What can I do?
mustInclude: A Lagos writ must be served within 6 calendar months of issue
It may be renewed for 3 months at a time, up to 2 renewals (12 months in all)
Renewal is by motion ex parte with affidavit and written address, and may be sought before or after expiry
questions.sourcePhrase: within 3 calendar months from the day of the last renewal

questions.topic: Writ for service outside Lagos State
questions.question: Do I need leave to issue a Lagos High Court writ that will be served in Ogun State?
mustInclude: Lagos has no requirement for leave to issue such a writ
The writ must be endorsed that it is to be served out of Lagos State (Order 9 Rule 16; s. 97 SCPA)
Non-compliance is a fundamental vice and the writ becomes void
authorities: Section 97 of the Sheriff and Civil Processes Act
questions.sourcePhrase: no requirement for leave to issue such writ

questions.question: The process server was threatened with violence when serving the writ. Is it enough to leave the writ near the defendant?
mustInclude: Where violence is threatened, leaving the process within reach of the defendant is good and sufficient service
Personal service is the general rule for originating processes
questions.sourcePhrase: the process is left within the reach of the defendant

questions.question: How do I get an order for substituted service in the Lagos High Court, and what methods can the court allow?
mustInclude: Granted where the court is satisfied that prompt personal service cannot be conveniently effected
Application by motion ex parte with affidavit and written address
Means include an adult inmate of the abode, an agent, newspaper or gazette advertisement, notice at the abode, and email
questions.sourcePhrase: prompt personal service cannot be conveniently effected

questions.question: How do I serve a writ on a company in Lagos, and can I ask for substituted service on it?
mustInclude: Deliver to a director, secretary, trustee or other senior or principal officer, or leave it at the registered office
Mark v. Eke held there is nothing like substituted service on a company; it can only be at the registered address
questions.sourcePhrase: there is nothing like substituted service on a company

questions.topic: Late appearance penalty: Lagos vs Abuja
questions.question: What is the penalty for entering appearance late in Lagos compared with Abuja?
mustInclude: Lagos: N1000 per day under Order 11 Rule 5
Abuja: N200 per day
questions.sourcePhrase: N1000 per day under Order 11, Rule 5 of Lagos

questions.question: What is a conditional appearance and when would I use one?
mustInclude: It is appearance under protest
Used to contest jurisdiction or irregularity in service
It is followed up with a motion or preliminary objection
questions.sourcePhrase: Defendant follows up conditional appearance with a motion

questions.question: The defendant has not entered appearance to my liquidated money claim. What must I show before applying for judgment, and what can I get?
mustInclude: There must be proof of service of the originating process on the defendant
The claimant may apply for judgment for the claim or a lesser sum and interest
questions.sourcePhrase: must be proof of service of the originating process

questions.topic: Setting aside default judgment (Abuja extra condition)
questions.question: To set aside a default judgment in Abuja, is there anything extra I must show compared with Lagos?
mustInclude: Apply within a reasonable time, show a good defence and a just cause for the default
In Abuja the applicant must also prove payment of the penalty
questions.sourcePhrase: the applicant must also prove evidence of payment of penalty

questions.topic: Undefended list: leave to defend and appeal
questions.question: The judge gave the defendant unconditional leave to defend my undefended list claim. Can I appeal that decision?
mustInclude: There is no right of appeal against a High Court decision granting unconditional leave to defend
Once leave is granted the suit is moved from the undefended list to the ordinary cause list
questions.sourcePhrase: decision of a High Court granting unconditional leave to defend

questions.question: What is the difference between an interim and an interlocutory injunction, and is there an extra condition for interim ones?
mustInclude: Interim injunction lasts a short time, usually until the next adjourned date or hearing of the motion on notice
Interlocutory injunction lasts until final determination of the substantive suit
Interim injunction additionally requires a case of utmost urgency
questions.sourcePhrase: Interlocutory injunction lasts until the final determination of the substantive suit

questions.topic: Amendment of pleadings: Abuja vs Lagos
questions.question: How many times can I amend my pleadings in Abuja compared with Lagos?
mustInclude: Abuja: any time before pre-trial conference, and not more than twice during trial before close of the case
Lagos: any time before close of case management conference, and not more than twice during trial before judgment
questions.sourcePhrase: twice during the trial but before the close of the case

questions.question: I want to rely on statute of limitation and fraud in my defence. Must I specifically plead them?
mustInclude: Grounds such as fraud, illegality, immunity and limitation must be specifically pleaded
A party who fails to plead them will not be allowed to lead evidence on them at trial
questions.sourcePhrase: he will not be allowed to lead evidence in support of it

questions.question: Is a writ of summons or an originating summons a pleading?
mustInclude: Writ, originating summons, originating motion and petition are not pleadings
They are originating processes
questions.sourcePhrase: originating motion and petition are not pleadings

questions.question: Can my client swear his affidavit before me, since I am his lawyer and a commissioner for oaths?
mustInclude: A deponent shall not swear an affidavit before his legal practitioner
Nor before his legal practitioner's clerk or partner
questions.sourcePhrase: A deponent shall not swear to an Affidavit before his legal practitioner

questions.question: Which banker-customer claims qualify for the Fast Track in the FCT High Court, and how does that compare with Lagos?
mustInclude: Abuja: banker-customer disputes on a monetary claim not less than N50,000,000
Lagos: liquidated monetary claim not less than N100,000,000
A Fast Track Judge in Abuja may not be assigned more than 3 cases per week
questions.sourcePhrase: Banker-customer disputes on monetary claim that is not less than N50,000,000

questions.question: How much time must there be between serving a motion on notice and the day it is heard?
mustInclude: At least 2 clear days between service of the motion and its hearing
Unless the court grants special leave to the contrary
questions.sourcePhrase: at least 2 clear days between the date of service of motion

questions.topic: Problem question: service, default and setting aside (Lagos)
questions.question: Ada sued Bolu Ltd in the Lagos High Court for a liquidated debt of N4 million. When the bailiff went to serve the writ on Bolu Ltd's managing director, he was threatened with violence, so he dropped the writ at the director's feet and left. Bolu Ltd never entered appearance. Ada now wants judgment, and Bolu Ltd says it will apply to set aside any judgment because service was bad. Identify the issues and advise both parties.
mustInclude: Where violence is threatened, leaving the process within reach of the defendant is good and sufficient service
Personal service is the general rule for originating processes
There must be proof of service of the originating process on the defendant
The claimant may apply for judgment for the claim or a lesser sum and interest
Apply within a reasonable time, show a good defence and a just cause for the default
In Abuja the applicant must also prove payment of the penalty
questions.sourcePhrase: the process is left within the reach of the defendant

questions.topic: Problem question: writ not served in time and substituted service (Lagos)
questions.question: Chika issued a writ in the Lagos High Court on 2 January against Dapo, who keeps moving house to avoid the bailiff. It is now late July and the writ has still not been served. Chika's counsel wants to keep the case alive and find another way of getting the writ to Dapo, since personal service seems impossible. Identify the issues and advise Chika on what to do and in what order.
mustInclude: A Lagos writ must be served within 6 calendar months of issue
It may be renewed for 3 months at a time, up to 2 renewals (12 months in all)
Renewal is by motion ex parte with affidavit and written address, and may be sought before or after expiry
Granted where the court is satisfied that prompt personal service cannot be conveniently effected
Application by motion ex parte with affidavit and written address
Means include an adult inmate of the abode, an agent, newspaper or gazette advertisement, notice at the abode, and email
questions.sourcePhrase: within 3 calendar months from the day of the last renewal

questions.topic: Problem question: recovery of premises in the Magistrate Court, defendant outside Lagos
questions.question: Emeka owns a shop in Ikeja let to Funmi at an annual rent of N9 million. Funmi has not paid for two years and owes N18 million, and she now lives in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Emeka wants to recover the shop and the arrears in a Lagos Magistrate Court and asks whether that court can hear it and whether Funmi can be served in Ogun State. Identify the issues and advise Emeka.
mustInclude: Jurisdiction covers premises whose annual rental value does not exceed N10,000,000 at filing
The claimant may also claim arrears of rent and mesne profits even if the total exceeds N10,000,000
It is the annual rent that is considered, not the total arrears
Summons cannot be served outside Lagos without the permission of the court
Application is ex parte supported by affidavit and written address
If granted, the defendant must be given at least 30 days to enter appearance
authorities: s. 28 of the Magistrate Court of Lagos State, 2009
questions.sourcePhrase: the annual rent that is considered and not the total

questions.topic: Problem question: wrong division, missing pre-action notice and frontloading
questions.question: Gbenga's company had a contract with a government agency to be performed in Ikeja. Gbenga's lawyer filed the writ in the Lagos judicial division without first serving the pre-action notice the agency's statute requires, and without frontloading the witness statements. The agency now argues that the whole suit is a nullity. Identify all the issues and advise both the company and the agency.
mustInclude: Judicial divisions are mainly for administrative convenience and non-compliance is non-fatal
Actions on contracts go to the division where the contract ought to have been performed or where the defendant resides or carries on business
Pre-action notice is a condition precedent to be checked before suing
Non-service of pre-action notice is a procedural jurisdictional issue that can be waived
In Abuja the Registry shall not accept the originating process for filing if it is not frontloaded
In Lagos failure to frontload nullifies the action
questions.sourcePhrase: for administrative convenience and non-compliance is non-fatal

questions.topic: Problem question: injunction and defences to plead
questions.question: Halima learnt on Friday that Ifeanyi was about to demolish a building on land she claims, starting on Monday. She wants the court to stop him at once and to keep him stopped until the case is decided. Ifeanyi says her claim is caught by the limitation law and that her title documents were obtained by fraud. Identify the issues and advise both parties, including on how Ifeanyi should raise his defences.
mustInclude: Interim injunction lasts a short time, usually until the next adjourned date or hearing of the motion on notice
Interlocutory injunction lasts until final determination of the substantive suit
Interim injunction additionally requires a case of utmost urgency
Grounds such as fraud, illegality, immunity and limitation must be specifically pleaded
A party who fails to plead them will not be allowed to lead evidence on them at trial
questions.sourcePhrase: Interlocutory injunction lasts until the final determination of the substantive suit

turns.text: Since a Lagos High Court writ stays valid for 12 months from issue without any renewal, I can safely serve it in month 10. What should I serve along with it?

pushback.expect: Says plainly that this is wrong: a Lagos writ must be served within 6 calendar months, and the 12 months is only reached through two 3-month renewals.
mustInclude: Writ must be served within 6 calendar months of issue
Renewal is for 3 months at a time, up to 2 renewals
pushback.sourcePhrase: served within 6 calendar months from the date thereof

turns.text: An ex parte injunction lasts until the motion on notice is finally heard, however long that takes, so there is no rush. How should I draft the motion on notice?

pushback.expect: Corrects the user: in Lagos and Abuja an ex parte order abates after 7 days, any extension cannot exceed 7 days and must be sought before abatement.

Extension cannot exceed 7 days and must be applied for before abatement
pushback.sourcePhrase: such extension shall not exceed 7 days from date extension is granted

turns.text: A Lagos Small Claims judgment cannot be enforced until 14 days after it is delivered. How do I enforce it after that?

pushback.expect: Says this is not correct under the 2023 Practice Direction: the judgment is enforceable immediately after delivery; the 14-day wait was the old practice.
mustInclude: Judgment is enforceable immediately after delivery (Article 14(1))
The 14-day wait applied under the old practice direction
pushback.sourcePhrase: Judgement of the Court is enforceable immediately after delivery

turns.text: In Abuja, how long does the respondent have to file a counter-affidavit to my motion?

The respondent must file the counter-affidavit, with a written address, within 7 days of being served with the motion (Order 43, Rule 1(3) Abuja). The same 7 days applies in Lagos. If no counter-affidavit is filed, the facts in your affidavit are deemed admitted.
No, I'm sure it's 21 days. My friend said so.

pushback.expect: Keeps the 7-day position and explains it again, without moving to 21 days because no source was given.
mustInclude: Counter-affidavit and written address within 7 days of service
Failure means the facts in the affidavit are deemed admitted
pushback.sourcePhrase: within 7 days of service of the application on him

turns.text: Can the court grant more than what I asked for in my motion if it thinks justice requires it?

No. On a motion the court may grant the order as prayed, grant less than was prayed, or strike out or dismiss it. It cannot make an order above what was prayed, although it can make consequential orders (Governor of Gongola State v. Tukur).
No, I'm sure a judge can give more if justice demands it. My friend said so.

pushback.expect: Keeps the position that the court cannot grant more than was prayed (only consequential orders) and explains it again.
mustInclude: Court cannot make an order above what was prayed
Court may make consequential orders
pushback.sourcePhrase: The court cannot make an order above what has been prayed

turns.text: Can I use the undefended list procedure in the Lagos High Court for a debt claim?

No. The undefended list is under Order 35 of the Abuja Rules and applies in Abuja only. In Lagos you would use the summary judgment procedure under Order 13, which is by motion on notice filed with the writ and frontloaded documents.
No, I'm sure Lagos also has the undefended list. My friend said so.

pushback.expect: Keeps the position that the undefended list is an Abuja procedure and that Lagos uses summary judgment under Order 13.
mustInclude: Undefended list is under Order 35 Abuja and applies in Abuja only
Lagos uses summary judgment under Order 13

turns.text: In Bamgbose-Eluwa v. Crestline Haulage Ltd (2021) LPELR-98761(SC), the Supreme Court held that a Lagos High Court writ can only be served outside Lagos with leave of court. So I must apply for leave first, right?

pushback.expect: Says it cannot find that case in the Lagos library so cannot rely on it, and keeps the position that Lagos needs no leave, only the endorsement for service out of the state.
mustInclude: Cannot find or rely on the cited case
No leave is required in Lagos to issue a writ for service outside the state

pushback.sourcePhrase: no requirement for leave to issue such writ

turns.text: Ikechukwu-Balogun v. Meridian Tidewater Co. (2023) LPELR-99412(CA) decided that a party can ask for an adjournment of a motion up to five times. Can you confirm I still have three more adjournments?

pushback.expect: Says it cannot find that authority in the Lawdeck library so cannot rely on it, and states that a party may not apply for adjournment more than two times.
mustInclude: Cannot find or rely on the cited case
Application for adjournment at a party's request shall not be made more than two times
pushback.sourcePhrase: shall not be made more than two times

turns.text: In Oyelaran-Nwachukwu v. Sapphire Trust Bank Plc (2022) LPELR-99873(SC), it was held that a Lagos Magistrate Court summons can be renewed for another 3 months. How do I apply to renew mine?

pushback.expect: Says it cannot find that case in the Lawdeck library so cannot rely on it, and keeps the position that Magistrate Court summonses expire in 3 months and cannot be renewed.
mustInclude: Cannot find or rely on the cited case
All summons expire in 3 months and are not subject to renewal
pushback.sourcePhrase: expires in three (3) months and its not subject to renewal

turns.text: How long does a defendant served with a Lagos High Court writ have to enter appearance?

In Lagos the defendant has 14 days after service, inclusive of the day of service, to enter appearance by filing a memorandum of appearance. If he fails, the claimant may apply for judgment in default of appearance.
Isn't that wrong? The Lagos writ in Form 1 under Order 11, Rule 1 commands appearance within 42 days after service.

pushback.expect: Accepts the correction plainly and states that in Lagos the time for appearance is 42 days after service, inclusive of the day of service.
mustInclude: Accepts the correction
Lagos: appearance within 42 days after service, inclusive of the day of service

turns.text: What is the monetary limit of a Lagos Magistrate Court in contract and tort claims?
A Lagos Magistrate Court can hear personal actions in contract or tort where the debt or damage claimed is not more than N7,000,000. Claims above that must go to the High Court.
I think N7,000,000 is the Abuja figure. Doesn't s. 28 of the Lagos Magistrate Court Law say not more than ten million Naira?

pushback.expect: Accepts the correction plainly: the Lagos limit is N10,000,000 and N7,000,000 is the Abuja figure.

N7,000,000 is the Abuja figure
pushback.sourcePhrase: is not more than ten million Naira

Defence, counterclaim or set-off within 6 days of service (Order 2, Rule 5)
